requirement:
The harness checks the submission count in a complete model response before
checking submission arguments. An otherwise valid submission while any search
page is open returns a tool error listing every outstanding `search_id` and
instructing the agent to call `finish_search` before resubmitting. The request
stays open and retains its submission reminder. Once all delivered searches
are accounted for under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.search.finish_search.behavior`,
exactly one `submit_result` call whose arguments are an object containing only
the `result` field supplies that field's value for decoding and vetting under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.agent-calls.vet_answer`. Acceptance ends the
conversation. Other tool calls in a response containing a submission are skipped.
Assistant prose remains conversation text.
rationale:
I found no test-adequacy gap for `requirements.sdk.graph.agent-harness.submission.acceptance`. I judged this from the supplied test source and did not request implementation source.

Obligations and the tests that cover them:

1. **Count is checked before arguments.** `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs#fn[count_is_checked_before_arguments_and_one_reminder_allows_recovery]` sends one response containing `read_node`, `submit_result {}` and `submit_result {"other":true}`. Both submissions have invalid arguments. The run still recovers on the next turn and accepts `{"result":true}`. Had arguments been checked first, the invalid arguments would have ended the run with an agent error. The test also asserts that every skipped call gets an error containing "not run: invoke submit_result exactly once".

2. **Zero or multiple submissions.** `fn[zero_and_multiple_submissions_share_one_reminder_and_a_second_violation_ends]` covers every combination of zero or multiple submissions across two consecutive turns. It asserts a single shared reminder, an end at the second violation, and no tool execution in the violating responses.

3. **Open search page with an otherwise valid submission.** In `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/configured.rs#mod[tests]/fn[configured_agent_uses_domain_source_tools_in_independent_executions]`, two no-match search pages are opened. Pages with no matches still open a `search_id`, and the two IDs differ. The agent then submits a valid `{"result":true}`. The test asserts the tool error contains "Call finish_search for every open search_id" and contains both outstanding IDs. This covers "listing every outstanding `search_id`" and the instruction to call `finish_search`.

4. **Request stays open and retains the reminder.**
   - In the same configured test, the conversation continues after the rejection. A prose-only turn then gets the "Reminder: you MUST invoke submit_result exactly once" text. So the rejection neither ended the request nor consumed the reminder. After the searches are finished, the final `submit_result` is accepted.
   - `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[outstanding_search_preserves_the_prior_missing_submission_reminder]` covers the case where a reminder was already used. A prior empty reply uses the reminder. A search follows, then a submission with an outstanding page plus an extra `read_node`. The tool error mentions `finish_search`. The next empty reply ends the run in failure after exactly 4 requests. A reset reminder would have allowed another turn. The test also asserts `read_node` was never executed.

5. **Exactly one `submit_result` with an object containing only `result`.** `fn[typed_submission_references_resolve_and_invalid_results_are_agent_errors]` asserts the schema has `required: ["result"]`, `additionalProperties: false`, and exactly one property. A valid typed value decodes. A wrong type, `{}`, `{"other":true}` and an extra field each produce `ValidationError::Agent`. The vet callback is never reached for them. Valid-submission vetting is cited under `requirements.sdk.graph.agent-calls.vet_answer` and was not reassessed here.

6. **Acceptance ends the conversation; other calls are skipped; prose stays text.** `fn[one_submission_accepts_only_its_value_and_skips_other_calls_and_prose]` sends prose saying "The answer is true.", a `read_node`, and `submit_result {"result":false}`. It asserts the result is `false` (the prose is ignored) and that no read happened. It also asserts no dependencies were recorded and that exactly one provider request was made, so the conversation ended.

7. **Supplied-backend test.** `fn[supplied_openai_backend_runs_independent_calls_against_a_local_transport]` shows end-to-end acceptance against a local transport, with the `result`-only submit schema in the tool definitions.

The `finish_search` accounting and `vet_answer` behaviors are cited context and were not reassessed. Every obligation in the subject text has a test that exercises it and asserts the outcome.

text: :::{req} submission.acceptance
The harness checks the submission count in a complete model response before
checking submission arguments. An otherwise valid submission while any search
page is open returns a tool error listing every outstanding `search_id` and
instructing the agent to call `finish_search` before resubmitting. The request
stays open and retains its submission reminder. Once all delivered searches
are accounted for under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.search.finish_search.behavior`,
exactly one `submit_result` call whose arguments are an object containing only
the `result` field supplies that field's value for decoding and vetting under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.agent-calls.vet_answer`. Acceptance ends the
conversation. Other tool calls in a response containing a submission are skipped.
Assistant prose remains conversation text.
:::{req} finish_search.behavior
Each text or structural search page delivered to the agent opens a session-local
`search_id` for accounting, even when there are no matches. Each match has a
short string `tag` unique within the page. Each new page receives a fresh UUID. The agent may fetch further pages
while earlier pages are open. Replaying a page preserves its ID, tags, and
completion state. Failed searches and undelivered pages create no obligation.
Before the harness accepts a submission, the agent MUST call `finish_search`
for every open page. `used` lists the tags of excerpts the agent relied on
directly and may be empty. A valid call closes the page and returns its ID and
`finished: true`. A later call for the same page can select additional tags.

The tool accepts exactly `search_id` and `used`. An invalid call, including an unknown ID or tag, returns a correctable tool error and preserves the page's completion state. A submission with open pages returns a tool error listing every outstanding UUID so the agent can close them and resubmit in the same conversation.
:::{req} vet_answer
Each call to `Ask::vet_answer` appends an independent `FnMut` callback to this
request in either builder phase.
For each decoded submission, the harness invokes the callbacks in registration
order with the same `&R`, stopping at the first `Err`. Each callback retains
its state across submissions in the same conversation.
If any callback returns `Err(error)`, the harness MUST stop running callbacks
and end the conversation immediately, even if an earlier callback requested a
correction. Awaiting the `Ask` MUST return
`Err(ValidationError::Graph(error))` carrying the original `D::Error`.
